data.narrative: In Module 06 (Parallel Agent Management), Alekhya orchestrated a 3-agent parallel sprint across Comments, @Mention Parsing, and Audit Logging using an Interface-First strategy. When cross-feature integration revealed a communication gap between event emission and middleware interception, she diagnosed the protocol mismatch and engineered a surgical integration glue module (src/services/comment_audit_glue.js). The entire system converged to 38 passing tests with zero merge conflicts, demonstrating sophisticated multi-agent coordination.

dimension_scores.observation: Authored comprehensive parallel interface contracts defining isolated file domains, immutable references, and shared data shapes.
dimension_scores.evidence: Documented 3 agent contracts in progress/parallel-contracts.md eliminating file-level merge conflicts across all components.

dimension_scores.observation: Executed 3 levels of verification (individual components, cross-feature workflows, conflict detection), identifying the subtle event-bus vs middleware semantic mismatch.
dimension_scores.evidence: Penned tests/cross_feature_integration.test.js and tests/glue_integration.test.js to verify end-to-end data flow.

dimension_scores.observation: Resolved the cross-feature communication gap in a single targeted turn via an event-to-audit glue module rather than re-running entire agents.
dimension_scores.evidence: Authored src/services/comment_audit_glue.js, taking the suite to 38/38 passing tests in under 290ms.

dimension_scores.observation: Selected Option A (Interface-First) to prevent compounding merge tax, correctly recognizing that parallel agents require more upfront coordination, not less.
dimension_scores.evidence: Reasoned that upfront schema locking converts potential distributed integration nightmares into clean modular assembly.

dimension_scores.observation: Delivered a fully integrated multi-agent system where comments, mentions, audit logging, and activity feeds interoperate seamlessly.
dimension_scores.evidence: 38 automated unit and integration tests passing in tests/*.test.js with zero warnings or regressions.

Interface contract rigor: locks down input/output boundaries and communication protocols before launching parallel tasks.
Surgical integration engineering: bridges semantic integration gaps with minimal glue code rather than expensive full-task rewrites.
